stem: A closing Massachusetts pharmacy will move its Schedule II through VI stock to a sister pharmacy. The Manager of Record has given the Board written certified-mail notice with all required particulars and the transfer is set for day 15. Which statements about what follows are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The transferor may keep a small residual stock to finish outstanding prescriptions.
An attestation confirming the inventory is filed with the Board within 30 days.
The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances.
Only the transferee's Manager of Record needs to sign the inventory report.
The transferor may possess no controlled substances after the transfer date.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 6.14(2) requires the transferor to take a complete inventory on the transfer date of all Schedule II through V substances and all Schedule VI substances reportable to the prescription monitoring program, requires BOTH Managers of Record to sign it, requires an attestation with the Board WITHIN TEN DAYS, and provides that the transferor pharmacy may not possess any controlled substances after the transfer date.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation forecloses any possession after the transfer date.
choice_analysis.B: The attestation window is ten days, not thirty.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: reportable Schedule VI is inside the inventory.
choice_analysis.D: Both Managers of Record sign, subject to the unavailability substitution.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: a flat prohibition after the transfer date.

related_facts: A staff pharmacist may sign where the transferor Manager of Record is unavailable
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates carry the 14-day figure forward and use it for the attestation as well.

reasoning_steps: Separate the 14-day notice clock from the 10-day attestation clock
Read what the inventory must cover
